notes: Pass rate is 100% for both with_skill and without_skill on all 3 evals -- these assertions don't discriminate correctness for this skill. A capable general-purpose agent with full repo access reconstructs the same commands, invariants, and framing directly from the code (pocket_coffea/workflow.py, cuts.py) and repo docs (disappearing_tracks/CLAUDE.md) that the skill also draws from.

The real, consistent signal is efficiency: with_skill averaged 109.3s / 50.5k tokens vs. 285.8s / 67.0k tokens without_skill -- roughly 2.6x faster and 25% fewer tokens, holding across all 3 evals individually, not just in aggregate.

Eval 3 (dissertation-silence-not-rejection) shows the largest efficiency gap (58.6s vs 146.5s, ~2.5x) because the skill's own 'Why this mode exists right now' section already contains the dissertation citation pre-digested; the baseline had to independently open and grep the actual DissertationFinal.pdf to reach the same conclusion.

Both without_skill runs for eval 2 (missing-fiducial-maps-trust-check) independently discovered something neither the with_skill run nor the packaged skill currently states: the --full-cutflow output's 'track_fiducialECAL' row is a different, static branch (isFiducialECALTrack) unrelated to the dynamic lepton fiducial-map veto, so there is no existing diagnostic that reveals whether the maps actually loaded. Worth adding to the skill's troubleshooting content.

Both without_skill runs for eval 1 independently flagged the same real-world gaps in the actual checkout: no muon fiducial map file exists at all, and the electron map is named without the '_v2' suffix the docs/skill examples use. This is a genuine blocker for actually running signal_acceptance today, not an eval artifact.

Recommendation for a future iteration: either raise the difficulty of these 3 evals (test something only the skill's authored content captures, not the underlying code/docs) or add efficiency thresholds as the primary pass/fail signal, since correctness parity with a thorough baseline is expected whenever the underlying repo is this well-documented.
